title: perf(canary): adaptive auto-detection and hysteresis for rollback guards
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves performance canary detection sensitivity and adds hysteresis to rollout guards to reduce flapping; includes metrics/alerts and docs; no user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: we continue to see noisy canary rollouts where transient latency spikes cause unnecessary rollbacks and human intervention. This change introduces adaptive auto-detection of regressions with workload-aware sensitivity and a hysteresis layer in the rollout guards so the system is less likely to flip on short-lived noise while still catching true regressions. What this PR does: 1) adaptive detector: replaces fixed-percent thresholds with rolling-window detection that adapts thresholds based on baseline variance and per-model traffic patterns; 2) hysteresis policy: implements configurable entry and exit margins for canary triggers (e.g. require sustained breach for X minutes or Y samples and an exit condition that avoids immediate re-promotion); 3) KV/Cache-aware signals: adds a detector that tracks KV-cache hit-rate regressions and uses them as secondary signals to avoid false positives during cold-cache events; 4) telemetry and alerts: emits new canary metrics (canary.detector.score, canary.hysteresis.state, canary.kv.hit_rate.delta) and dashboards; 5) testing & CI: adds unit and integration tests that simulate latency noise, KV cold-starts, and steady regressions; 6) docs & ops: updates perf-canary docs and runbook with recommended values. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2145) - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests in perf-canary lab - [x] dashboard and alert queries - [x] rollout plan and staged rollout flags - [x] updated runbook and runbooks/docs link. Backwards compatibility: all changes opt-in via canary policy flags; default behavior remains safe for existing customers. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag starting with internal clusters (2 days), then Canary control plane (7 days), then default for new model rollouts if no regressions observed. Performance: detector runs are micro-batched and off the hot path; CPU overhead is negligible based on local bench. Related: ENG-3120 (improved canary telemetry), SUP-403 (customer incident that motivated hysteresis tuning).
